_comment: Retired citation identifiers. Each entry was a live citation in this repository
until the 2026-09-10 dataset identity remediation (commit C1). They still appear
in the tree, but only inside comments that document the defect. scripts/check_dois.py
allows an occurrence of a retired identifier ONLY on a line that marks it as
documentation; putting one back into service as a live citation fails the gate
ORACLES, per entry, stated exactly. Every entry here was resolved 2026-09-10 with
the doi.org Handle System (/api/handles), which is registry-agnostic and therefore
the authoritative existence check for CrossRef, DataCite, Zenodo and wwPDB alike;
all seven returned responseCode 100 (handle not found). The four 10.1021/10.1093
entries were ADDITIONALLY probed against CrossRef /works and returned 404, a second
independent oracle. The three 10.5281/zenodo.* entries were NOT probed against
CrossRef and deliberately so: Zenodo DOIs are minted through DataCite, so a CrossRef
404 would carry no information about them. Their dispositive evidence is syntactic -
a Zenodo suffix is a numeric record id, so a word suffix is not a DOI at all and
cannot resolve at any registry. Positive control 10.1021/jm061277y resolved and the
negative control did not, in the same check, so a blocked or rate-limited host is
excluded as the cause of the responseCode 100 results.

10.5281/zenodo.dude37.reason: Zenodo DOIs carry a numeric record id; a word suffix is not DOI syntax and can never resolve.

10.5281/zenodo.itc187.reason: Zenodo DOIs carry a numeric record id; a word suffix is not DOI syntax and can never resolve.
10.5281/zenodo.itc187.action: emptied; dataset is declared NRGlab-internal with no published deposit

10.5281/zenodo.muv2009.reason: Zenodo DOIs carry a numeric record id; a word suffix is not DOI syntax and can never resolve.

10.1021/ci800224j.reason: Valid DOI syntax but not registered: Handle responseCode 100, CrossRef /works 404.
10.1021/ci800224j.replacement_evidence: CrossRef bibliographic search, exact title match: Verdonk et al., 'Protein-Ligand Docking against Non-Native Protein Conformers', J. Chem. Inf. Model. 48:2214-2225 (2008) - the paper the surrounding citation text names.

10.1021/ci8003380.reason: Valid DOI syntax but not registered: Handle responseCode 100, CrossRef /works 404.
10.1021/ci8003380.replacement_evidence: CrossRef bibliographic search, exact title match: Rohrer & Baumann, 'Maximum Unbiased Validation (MUV) Data Sets for Virtual Screening Based on PubChem Bioactivity Data', J. Chem. Inf. Model. 49:169-184 (2009).

10.1093/nar/g1271.reason: Valid DOI syntax but not registered: Handle responseCode 100, CrossRef /works 404. Not named by the original audit; found by the repo-wide sweep.
10.1093/nar/g1271.replacement_evidence: CrossRef bibliographic search, exact title match for the database the entry names: Yang, Roy & Zhang, 'BioLiP: a semi-manually curated database for biologically relevant ligand-protein interactions', Nucleic Acids Res. 41:D1096-D1103. If the BioLiP2 update is intended instead, 10.1093/nar/gkad630 is the verified alternative.

10.1021/ci100366a.reason: Valid DOI syntax but not registered: Handle responseCode 100, CrossRef /works 404. Not named by the original audit; found by the repo-wide sweep.
10.1021/ci100366a.replacement_evidence: The entry names two different CSAR releases ('CSAR-NRC HiQ 2010 / CSAR 2012') and no single paper covers both. Verified-registered candidates considered and rejected: 10.1021/ci200082t (Dunbar et al. 2011, CSAR Benchmark Exercise of 2010, JCIM 51:2036-2046) covers only the 2010/HiQ release; 10.1021/ci100036a resolves but to an unrelated MM-PB/SA paper despite being one digit-transposition away. No DOI was invented.
